run.question: A customer reported an order failure with trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR. Can you search across all our app-190-service-* indexes to trace the request flow and find where the error originated? What error code was returned?

report.summary: The customer trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR is present in the Elasticsearch logs of the app-190-service-* indices (four indices exist: app-190-service-auth, -gateway, -inventory, -orders). Six documents carry that exact trace_id, all with @timestamp 2026-11-23T17:25:00.000Z-17:25:00.140Z, and they show the request flow gateway -> auth -> orders -> inventory -> orders -> gateway. The error originated in the inventory service: at 17:25:00.080Z it logged level ERROR, error_code INV-ERR-4082, "Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23". The orders service then logged ORD-ERR-1001 ("Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082") at 17:25:00.130Z and the gateway logged GW-ERR-400 ("Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled") at 17:25:00.140Z. So the error code returned to the caller was HTTP 400 Bad Request, recorded as GW-ERR-400, with the originating code INV-ERR-4082 on the inventory service and ORD-ERR-1001 in between. Across the whole authorized month window only these three ERROR-level documents matched in the app-190-service-* indices, all on this trace, and inventory logged 21 other "Stock reserved successfully" INFO lines between 17:15 and 17:35, so this is an isolated rejection rather than a broad inventory outage. Jaeger could not be used to confirm the span-level chain (the supplied ID is not a valid hex trace ID), and Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error-rate and latency metrics for these services could not be checked.

claims.text: Four Elasticsearch indices match app-190-service-*: app-190-service-auth (51 docs, health green), app-190-service-gateway (52 docs, green), app-190-service-inventory (51 docs, green) and app-190-service-orders (52 docs, green).
All four app-190-service-* indices map the same fields: @timestamp, duration_ms, error_code, level, message, service, span_id, trace_id.

A search for the literal value "TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR" across app-190-service-* returned 6 documents (total 6, shards 4/4 successful), ordered by timestamp: gateway INFO "Received request POST /api/orders for user_12847" (span-gw-err, 17:25:00.000Z, 2 ms); auth INFO "User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token" (span-auth-err, 17:25:00.010Z, 15 ms); orders INFO "Processing order for product SKU-78234, quantity: 500" (span-orders-err, 17:25:00.030Z, 25 ms); inventory ERROR INV-ERR-4082 (span-inv-err, 17:25:00.080Z, 45 ms); orders ERROR ORD-ERR-1001 (span-orders-err-2, 17:25:00.130Z, 130 ms); gateway ERROR GW-ERR-400 (span-gw-err-2, 17:25:00.140Z, 145 ms).

The originating error log is from service "inventory" in index app-190-service-inventory at 2026-11-23T17:25:00.080Z: level ERROR, error_code INV-ERR-4082, message "Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23", span_id span-inv-err, trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR.
The orders service logged error_code ORD-ERR-1001 at 2026-11-23T17:25:00.130Z with message "Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082" on the same trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR.

The gateway logged error_code GW-ERR-400 at 2026-11-23T17:25:00.140Z with message "Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled" on trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR, i.e. the code returned to the caller was HTTP 400 Bad Request.

Over the whole authorized window (2026-10-24T17:51:08Z to 2026-11-23T17:51:08Z) only 3 documents with level=ERROR matched in app-190-service-* and all three belong to trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR (INV-ERR-4082, ORD-ERR-1001, GW-ERR-400); the same 3 documents were the only ERROR rows in the default 1-hour window ending 2026-11-23T17:51:08Z.

In app-190-service-inventory between 17:15:00Z and 17:35:00Z on 2026-11-23, 22 documents were returned: 21 are level INFO "Stock reserved successfully" (span-inv-15 to span-inv-35) and the single ERROR is the INV-ERR-4082 span-inv-err line; a successful reservation was logged at the same second, 17:25:00.080Z (span-inv-25, trace_id TRACE-24647).

In app-190-service-orders between 17:20:00Z and 17:30:00Z on 2026-11-23, 13 documents were returned and every other minute's entry is level INFO "Order created, checking inventory"; the only ERROR row in that index and window is ORD-ERR-1001 on TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR.

Authentication failure was considered and rejected: the auth service logged level INFO "User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token" at 17:25:00.010Z on the same trace, before the order was processed, and no error_code is recorded on that span.

The gateway and orders as the origin of the failure were considered and rejected as origins: both of their error messages explicitly attribute the failure to the inventory result (orders: "inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082"; gateway: "Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled"), and their timestamps follow the inventory error at 17:25:00.080Z.

The failure mechanism is a business-rule/data rejection inside the inventory service's stock reservation (requested 500 units of SKU-78234 against 23 available), not an infrastructure or dependency failure of inventory: the message is an explicit insufficient-inventory condition, no timeout, connection or 5xx signal appears on this trace, and inventory continued to log successful reservations immediately before and after. Confirmation would need the SKU stock data and inventory error-rate metrics, which were not available in this Run.

Verify the stock record for SKU-78234 in the inventory system (23 available vs 500 requested) and whether a 400 rejection is the intended contract for insufficient stock, before treating this as a service defect; also re-check inventory error-rate/latency metrics once Prometheus is reachable.

gaps: Jaeger could not confirm the span-level chain: traces_query_trace_by_id for TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR returned INVALID_PARAMS (the ID is not hexadecimal), and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no Jaeger span/parent references were obtained; the flow above is reconstructed from Elasticsearch log documents, not spans.

Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for service_name label discovery on traces_span_metrics_calls_total, so no error-rate, request-rate or latency metrics for auth, gateway, orders or inventory could be checked; ERROR-level series for these services are unknown, not zero.

A cluster pod query over all namespaces returned 0 of 32 pods matching names like inventory/orders/gateway/auth (status no_data), so the Kubernetes objects, restarts, events and container logs of the app-190 services were not observable here; the cluster seen is otel-demo, not app-190.

The inventory stock level itself (SKU-78234, 23 units) is only known from the error message; no inventory/catalog data source was available to verify it or to see when stock fell below the requested quantity.

Terms aggregations on service.keyword and error_code.keyword returned empty buckets, so error-code distribution by service could not be aggregated; the conclusions about which services errored rest on the returned documents only.
No change history integration is available in this Run, so whether a stock change, configuration change or deployment preceded 17:25:00Z could not be checked.
next_steps: Confirm SKU-78234 stock and reservation policy with the inventory owners, and whether partial fulfillment or a different status code is expected.
Retry Jaeger lookup with the hexadecimal trace ID if the customer can supply it, to obtain span-level parent/child evidence for gateway -> orders -> inventory.
Once Prometheus is reachable, check error-rate and latency for the gateway, orders and inventory services around 2026-11-23T17:25:00Z to size the blast radius beyond this single trace.
